note: Events of the island game (Phase 2): campaigns, sieges, supply, plague, mercenaries, embassies, Sicels and Italian Greeks, Carthage's council and its houses, and towns changing sides. Same shape as data/events.json, plus 'places' (the towns an event is about), parts played by the generated cast ('census') or Carthage's named men ('punic'), and an 'island' block in 'when' for cities, armies and Carthage. History comes in as conditions, never dates (design council V8). They fire only in island games, from their own draw each season. The engine is src/core/events.ts with src/core/island-events.ts; the research card is docs/research/island-events.md.

rumors.note: Switch falseRumors only: the share of rumors from Carthage that are false, and how many seasons until word comes whether a rumor was true.

events.name: The mole to the island

facts.quote: It also had a narrow artificial causeway extending to the shore of Sicily, which the Motyans breached at this time

facts.text: Dionysius filled the strait and advanced his engines along the mole.
facts.quote: he at once put many times more men on the task of filling up the strait between the city and the coast, and, as the mole was extended, advanced his engines of war little by little toward the walls

failure.text: Your ships are rammed as they come out, one by one.

Lift the siege before it spreads

events.name: Plague in the Punic camp

facts.quote: This man possessed the strongest armament of any of the tyrants of Sicily at that time after Dionysius

facts.text: Dionysius entered the city with a small company and won him with the promise of land.
facts.quote: after entering the city with a small company, persuaded Agyris to join him as a genuine ally and promised to make him a present of a large portion of neighbouring territory

invented: trigger (Carthage's army in the interior; the source tells it of Magon's campaign)

events.name: The Sicels waver
events.text: The Sicels of the hills, who have hated you from of old, see Carthage's great army and talk of going over to it in a body.
events.why: Carthage's army is on the island, and the Sicels see their chance

choices.label: Strengthen the forts and store the harvest in the citadels of {town}
choices.text: The Sicels go over to Carthage, but your forts are full and the grain of the plain is behind walls.

effects.why: the harvest of the plain is stored there

choices.label: Offer the Sicels land to stay out of it
choices.text: Most of the Sicels take your land and stay in their hills.

choices.label: Let them go

facts.text: The Sicels, who had long hated Dionysius, went over to Carthage, all but Assorus; he strengthened the forts and stored the Leontine harvest in its citadels.
facts.quote: The Siceli, who had hated Dionysius from of old and now had an opportunity to revolt, went over in a body, with the exception of the people of Assorus, to the Carthaginians

facts.text: He was most concerned to fortify the citadels of Leontini and store the harvest of the plains there.
facts.quote: He was most concerned, however, to fortify the citadels of the Leontines and to store in them the harvest from the plains

invented: all numbers (the Sicels are shown as men joining Carthage's army)

events.name: The hill of Taurus
events.text: Sicels have walled the steep hill of Taurus above the old land of Naxos, near {town}. They say the hill was their fathers' before the Greeks came, and they mean to keep it.
events.why: your army is in the field, and the Sicels on Taurus sit across the coast road

choices.label: Storm the heights on a stormy winter night

mods.label: they guard the steep side carelessly

success.text: Your men climb through the snow, take the peak and hold it. The Sicels come down to make terms.

failure.text: Your men break into the town and are thrown out again from the higher ground. More than 600 die. You come down with nothing but your breastplate.

effects.why: beaten on the heights of Taurus

choices.label: Make a treaty and leave them their hill
Leave them be

effects.why: Sicel raiders on the coast road

facts.text: Sicels walled the peak of Taurus and named it Tauromenium.
facts.quote: since those who gathered remained ( menein ) upon Taurus, they named the city Tauromenium

facts.text: The Sicels held that the land had been their ancestors' before the Greeks founded Naxos.
facts.quote: that these parts of the island had been the possession of the Siceli, when Greeks first landed there and founded Naxos

facts.text: Dionysius attacked on a moonless stormy winter night, broke in, and was thrown out; more than six hundred died.
facts.quote: more than six hundred of Dionysius' troops were slain and most of them lost their complete armour, while Dionysius himself saved only his corslet

events.note: A failure here counts as a lost battle, so towns that do not love you may drive out your friends (Diodorus 14.88.5, the event 'Your friends driven out').

events.name: The Sicel lords
events.text: The war with Carthage is over, and the Sicel towns of the interior lie between your land and Carthage's. Their lords, Agyris of Agyrium, Damon of Centuripa, and the men of Herbita and Assorus, wait to see what you will do.
events.why: peace with Carthage leaves the interior open

choices.label: Campaign against the Sicel towns

success.text: You take Menaenum and Morgantina by force and others by treachery.

failure.text: The Sicels hold their hills.

choices.label: Make treaties with their lords

effects.why: the Sicel markets open to you
the Sicels will not open their roads to Carthage

choices.label: Leave the interior alone

facts.text: After the war Dionysius campaigned against the Sicels, took Menaenum and Morgantina, and made treaties with Agyris, Damon and the Herbitaeans and Assorini.
facts.quote: in the course of which he took Menaenum and Morgantinum and struck a treaty with Agyris, the tyrant of the Agyrinaeans, and Damon, the lord of the Centoripans

events.name: Archonides founds a city
events.text: Archonides, the leader of Herbita, has made peace with you. Now he takes his mercenaries, the refugees of your wars and Herbita's poor, and founds a new city on a hill by the sea, which he names Halaesa after himself.
events.why: your wars have filled the hills with refugees

choices.label: Hire his mercenaries away from him
Send gifts for the new city

effects.why: your name is honoured at Halaesa

choices.label: Let him build

facts.text: Archonides of Herbita, after peace with Dionysius, founded Halaesa with mercenaries and refugees.
facts.quote: For he had not only many mercenaries but also a mixed throng who had streamed into the city in connection with the war against Dionysius

facts.text: He occupied a hill eight stades from the sea and called the city Halaesa Archonidion.
facts.quote: he occupied a hill lying eight stades from the sea, on which he founded the city of Halaesa

invented: trigger (peace with Carthage, or three towns yours or allied)
events.note: Diodorus also reports that some said Halaesa was founded by the Carthaginians (14.16.4).

events.name: The Italian Greeks choose a general
events.text: Across the strait, the Greeks of Italy fear they are next. At Croton, full of Syracusan exiles, they choose {exile} as their general, because his hatred of you can be trusted.
events.why: your power reaches the strait, and {exile} is in exile

choices.label: Send gifts and land to your friends at Locri
choices.text: Locri stays with you, and the league is split.

choices.label: Strengthen Messana against a crossing
Let them gather

facts.text: The Italian Greeks gave Croton, with the most Syracusan exiles, the conduct of the war.
facts.quote: Since the city of the Crotoniates was the most heavily populated and had the largest number of exiles from Syracuse, they gave over to them the command of the war

facts.text: They chose Heloris as general, trusting his hatred of the tyrant.
facts.quote: chose as general Heloris the Syracusan. Since this man had been banished by Dionysius

invented: trigger (four or more towns yours or allied, and Heloris in exile)
events.note: Diodorus places this after 395; the game lets it happen whenever the situation arises. Italy stays names only in Phase 2.

events.name: A rumor from Carthage: the general on trial
events.text: Merchants from Carthage say that {accuser}, a man of the Hundred, has risen in the council to demand that {general} answer for the war. The general's friends are many, and so are his debts.
events.why: Carthage's war goes badly, and the Hundred judge their generals

choices.label: Send silver to {accuser}'s friends

success.text: The council strips {general} of his command.

failure.text: Your silver is traced back to Syracuse. The council closes ranks behind {general}.

effects.why: Syracusan silver found in the council

choices.label: Spread word that {general} is in your pay

success.text: The story takes. {General} is recalled to answer for it.

failure.text: No one in Carthage believes it.

choices.label: Let Carthage quarrel

events.note: The Hundred is the game's bloc from Aristotle, Politics 1273a, written decades later (see data/carthage.json). The accuser is one of the generated cast.
events.rumor: the Hundred meant to put {general} on trial

events.name: A rumor from Carthage: a merchant's word
events.text: A trader brings a quiet word from {elder}, head of one of Carthage's great merchant houses: spare Carthage's merchant ships, and he will speak for peace among the Elders.
events.why: the war costs the merchant houses dearly

choices.label: Promise to spare the merchant ships

effects.why: {elder} can show what peace is worth

choices.label: Seize his ships anyway
Send no answer

events.name: A rumor from Carthage: the dockyards cry for war
events.text: Word comes that {speaker}, who speaks for the dockyards in Carthage's assembly, has the crowd shouting for vengeance for the town you took.
events.why: you took a town of Carthage's own

choices.label: Send envoys to say you want only peace

success.text: The assembly hears your envoys out, and the shouting dies down.

failure.text: Your envoys are pelted in the street.

choices.label: Let them shout

events.rumor: {speaker} had the assembly crying for war

events.name: A rumor from Libya
events.text: A Greek trader back from Libya says the farmers there curse Carthage's levies and dues. A little silver, he says, would set the villages burning.
events.why: the Libyans are unhappy with Carthage

choices.label: Send agents with silver

mods.label: Carthage is at war and taking their sons

success.text: Your agents find willing ears in the villages.

failure.text: Your agents are caught and crucified at Carthage.

choices.label: Leave Libya alone

events.note: Diodorus tells of the Libyans' great rising after the war of 396 (14.77, not among the saved sections). This event is invention.
events.rumor: the Libyan villages were ready to rise

events.name: Carthage in mourning
events.text: Ships from Africa bring word that Carthage is in mourning. The city believes the gods are fighting it. It has voted to honour Demeter and Kore, whose temple its soldiers robbed, with priests from its first families and from the Greeks who live there.
events.why: Carthage lost its army in Sicily

choices.label: Send Greek priests and offerings for the new rites

effects.why: Syracuse honours the goddesses with them

choices.label: Let the city mock them

effects.why: the gods are on our side

choices.label: Say nothing

facts.text: Carthage was suddenly anxious for its own homeland.
facts.quote: of a sudden were forced to be anxious for their own fatherland

facts.text: The city was seized by superstitious fear and voted to propitiate the gods.
facts.quote: the entire city was seized by superstitious fear and dread

facts.text: They made their most renowned citizens priests of Demeter and Kore, and chose Greeks living among them to serve.
facts.quote: they appointed their most renowned citizens to be priests of these goddesses

invented: trigger (Carthage's army lost or sent home)

events.name: The captain of the garrison
events.text: {Captain}, whose company holds {town} for you, has been seen talking with a Punic merchant. Carthage's army is close.
events.why: Carthage's army is near {town}, and hired men are for sale

choices.label: Replace him with men from your guard
Pay his company a bonus
Trust him

success.text: {Captain} sends the merchant away.

failure.text: {Captain} opens the gates of {town} to Carthage.

events.name: A sally from the walls
events.text: Carthage's lines creep closer to the walls of {town} every day. The defenders say the enemy's siege works are badly guarded at night, and ask leave to sally out and burn them.
events.why: Carthage's army is besieging {town}

choices.label: Sally out by night and burn the works

success.text: The siege works burn, and the defenders come back with prisoners.

failure.text: The sally is caught in the open and cut to pieces before the gate.

choices.label: Run grain in by night to {town}
Hold the walls and wait

events.name: Talk of surrender
events.text: In besieged {town}, {leader} says openly that Syracuse will not come, and that it is better to make terms with Carthage now than to be sold after a storm.
events.why: {town} is besieged and no help has come

choices.label: Send word that your army is coming
Send silver to those who would hold out

effects.why: your silver strengthens the war party

choices.label: Let them decide

mods.label: the town is nearly out of grain

success.text: The assembly of {town} votes to hold out.

failure.text: {Leader} carries the assembly. {Town} opens its gates to Carthage.

events.name: Walls fallen down
events.text: Carthage's army is close to {town}, whose old walls have fallen down in places. Some of its people are already carrying their wives, children and goods away to other towns. Others recall an old oracle and are sure that all will be well.
events.why: Carthage's army is near {town}, and its walls are weak

choices.label: Pay to repair the walls in haste

effects.why: the walls are patched in haste

choices.label: Send men from your guard to hold it
Leave them to their oracle

facts.text: At Messana, with Himilcon near, the walls had fallen down and there was no time to repair them; families and goods were sent to neighbouring cities.
facts.quote: their walls had fallen down and that the situation allowed no time for their repair. Consequently they removed from the city their children and wives and most valuable possessions to neighbouring cities

facts.text: Others trusted an old oracle that Carthaginians would carry water in Messana.
facts.quote: Carthaginians must be bearers of water in

invented: trigger (any weakly walled town near Carthage's army; the source tells it of Messana)

events.name: Ships in the Great Harbour
events.text: Carthage's fleet rows into the Great Harbour in order, oars flashing, decked with spoils taken from your ships. Behind it come the merchantmen in their hundreds. The whole city watches from the walls in dismay.
events.why: Carthage's army and fleet have come to Syracuse

choices.label: Show yourself on the walls with your guard

effects.why: you stand on the walls with them

choices.label: Send fire-ships among them at night

success.text: Fire runs through the crowded anchorage.

failure.text: The fire-ships are towed aside and burn out harmlessly.

choices.label: Keep the gates shut

effects.why: dismay at the sight of the enemy fleet

facts.text: Himilcon's fleet, decked with spoils, entered the Great Harbour of Syracuse in order and dismayed the city.
facts.quote: Himilcon decked his ships with the spoils taken from the enemy and put in at the great harbour of the Syracusans, and he caused great dismay among the inhabitants of the city

invented: all numbers (Diodorus' 250 warships and 3,000 merchantmen are not used)

events.name: A general's offer
events.text: A slave comes to you by night from {town}. {Traitor}, who leads its men, will help you to the town if the price is right: great promises, and the safety of his kin.
events.why: the peace leaves you free to look at your neighbours, and {traitor} has seen which way the island is going

choices.label: Send him silver and your promise

effects.why: its first man is in your pay

choices.text: {Traitor} takes the silver. {town} now leans your way: if your army comes within reach, its gates may open.

choices.label: Send the slave home with nothing

facts.text: After the peace, Dionysius wanted the neighbouring Chalcidian cities.
facts.quote: was eager to attach to himself the neighbouring cities of the Chalcidians, namely, Naxos, Catanê, and Leontini

facts.text: Catana's general offered to betray the city to him.
facts.quote: for Arcesilaüs, the general of the Catanians, had offered to betray the city to him

facts.text: Naxos was handed over by its commander, won over by great promises.
facts.quote: Procles, the commander of the Naxians, on being won over by great promises, delivered over his native city to Dionysius

invented: trigger (any free town with a first man, in peacetime, while your army is at home)
the traitor is the town's first man from the generated cast
the town leaning your way instead of a set night

events.name: A herald before the walls
events.text: Your army stands within reach of {town}. You have no engines for a siege. Your officers say a herald might do what engines cannot: draw the army up in battle order where they can see it, and order {town} to hand over the city and take citizenship in Syracuse.
events.why: your army is in the field within reach of {town}

choices.label: Send the herald

success.text: {town} expects no help. Its people look at your lines, assent, and open their gates.

failure.text: {town} pays no attention to your herald and makes every preparation to stand a siege.

effects.why: they were ordered to give up their city

choices.label: Plunder their fields instead
choices.text: Your men strip the farms around {town} and drive the cattle home.

choices.label: Leave them be

facts.text: At Leontini Dionysius drew up his army and sent a herald ordering the city to surrender.
facts.quote: he at first led out his army in battle-order and dispatched a herald to the Leontines, commanding them to surrender the city

facts.text: The Leontines refused; with no engines, he gave up the siege and plundered their land.
facts.quote: Dionysius, having no engines of war, gave up the siege for the time being, but plundered their entire territory

facts.text: Later, ordered to hand over their city and take Syracusan citizenship, and fearing the fate of Naxos and Catana, the Leontines gave in.
facts.quote: he ordered them to hand over their city and enjoy citizenship in Syracuse

invented: trigger (any free or tributary town within six days of your army, in peacetime)
the odds, and the bonus once you have sacked a town

events.name: A man who would be tyrant
events.text: While your army is in the field near {town}, {climber} comes to your camp. He would make himself master of {town}, if you will back him, and he swears it will be your friend.
events.why: your army is near {town}, and {climber} sees a chance

choices.label: Back him with silver

success.text: {climber} seizes {town}. For now he keeps his word.

failure.text: {climber} takes {town}, then shuts its gates in your face. Other towns hear how your friends keep faith.

effects.why: a tyrant you set up shut his gates on you

choices.label: Tell the people of {town} what he plans

effects.why: you gave a would-be tyrant up to them

choices.text: The people of {town} stream into their market with their arms and deal with {climber} themselves. They remember who warned them.

choices.label: Send him away

facts.text: Near Enna, Dionysius persuaded a citizen, Aeimnestus, to bid for tyranny with his help.
facts.quote: he persuaded Aeimnestus, a native of the city, to make a bid for tyranny, promising to aid him in the undertaking

facts.text: Once in power, Aeimnestus did not let Dionysius in; Dionysius turned the Ennaeans against him.
facts.quote: did not admit Dionysius into the city, Dionysius in anger changed sides and urged the Ennaeans to overthrow the tyrant

facts.text: He did it to make other cities trust him.
facts.quote: because he wanted to encourage the other cities to put faith in him

invented: trigger (any free or tributary town near your army, in peacetime; Enna is not on the map)
the would-be tyrant is the town's first man from the generated cast, and he comes to you rather than you to him

events.name: What the war is for
events.text: The city is at war with Carthage. Your friends ask what you mean to win, so that they can tell the assembly and the allies. Whatever you choose will be the measure of the war: the chronicle will judge you by it.
events.why: a war has begun

choices.label: Drive Carthage from the west: take Motya or Panormus

effects.why: they smell the plunder of Carthage's own towns

choices.label: Free the Greek cities from Carthage's tribute

effects.why: a war to free the Greeks

choices.label: Hold what you have, and lose nothing

effects.why: a careful war spares their trade

invented: the whole matter: Dionysius' letter named what he wanted (Diodorus 14.47.2), the three aims are invention
events.note: Switch warFocus. Fired by war.ts when a war opens.

events.name: Peace envoys with terms
events.text: Carthage's envoys come to Syracuse with terms for a peace. What they offer follows from how the war has gone. You may take their terms, send them back for better ones, or send them home.
events.why: Carthage's council wants peace

choices.label: Take Carthage's terms
Send them back for the terms the war has earned

success.text: The envoys go home and come back with better terms. Peace is made.

failure.text: The envoys take offence and sail home. The war goes on.

effects.why: Carthage's envoys were sent home insulted

choices.label: Send them home: the war goes on

facts.text: In 392 the peace gave Dionysius the Sicels and Tauromenium.
facts.quote: The conditions were like the former except that the Siceli were to be subject to Dionysius and that he was to receive Tauromenium

invented: the terms are read from the war's ledger; their sizes are invention
the roll to press for better
events.note: Switch warFocus. Fired by war.ts when Carthage's peace act runs. The treaties of 392 and the 380s are patterns, not events of this decade.

events.name: The army wants battle
events.text: Your army has sat in the field for seasons with no battle. The allies' captains come to your tent: fight now, while we are here, or we go home to our harvests.
events.why: the army has been in the field for seasons without a battle

choices.label: Keep them with silver and promises
Tell them time and want will ruin the enemy without fighting

success.text: They grumble, but they stay.

failure.text: Angered, many of them leave for home and for the forts nearby.

effects.why: its men went home in anger

choices.label: Let the allies go home

facts.text: In 396 the Sicilian Greeks, angry that Dionysius would not fight, deserted him.
facts.quote: The majority of the Sicilian Greeks, being angered at his unwillingness to encounter the enemy, deserted Dionysius

facts.text: In 392 he said time and want would ruin the enemy; the Syracusans deserted him.
facts.quote: time and want would ruin the barbarians without fighting. Provoked to anger at this the Syracusans deserted him

invented: the trigger (seasons in the field without a battle)

events.name: A victor's welcome
events.text: {Victor} has beaten Carthage's army in the field, and you were not there. The soldiers cheer his name, and in the agora men say that when you are away even a small force is enough.
events.why: your army won a battle under {victor}

choices.label: Honour {victor} before the assembly
Take the credit yourself

effects.reason: you took the credit for his victory

choices.label: Reward him quietly with silver

facts.text: The Syracusans, having won without Dionysius, grew proud.
facts.quote: without his presence, had won a victory over the Carthaginians, they were now puffed up with pride

facts.text: Theodorus: when he is absent, even a small detachment is enough.
facts.quote: even a small detachment is sufficient

events.note: Switch warFocus. Fired by war.ts after a battle your army won under another man.

events.name: A truce of a few days
events.text: Beaten in the field, Carthage's general sends heralds: a truce of a few days, to bury the dead and to put your terms to his council at home.
events.why: you won a battle, and Carthage's army still stands

choices.label: Grant the truce

effects.why: its general drills his men through the truce

choices.label: Refuse: press them while they are beaten

invented: the whole matter is a pattern from the war of the 380s (Diodorus 15.16.1-2): there Carthage asked a truce and its new general drilled the army through it; it is not an event of 405 to 395
events.note: Switch warFocus. Fired by war.ts once a game, after you win a battle.

events.name: A gate from inside
events.text: A man slips out of {town} by night and comes to your tent. {Friend}, whose house is your friend inside the walls, will open a gate for you before dawn, for a price: silver now, and a place at the head of the town after.
events.why: a house inside {town} is your friend, and your army is at its walls

choices.label: Pay his price and take the gate

effects.why: the town remembers who sold it

choices.label: Refuse: you will take it by your own arms

facts.text: Arcesilaus, general of Catana, offered to betray his city to Dionysius.
facts.quote: had offered to betray the city to him

facts.text: Procles, general of Naxos, was bought.
facts.quote: won over by great promises

invented: the effect on the town's lean
